data.name: Forsythoside A

identifiers_status.reason: Gene and protein identifiers do not apply to the type "Drug".

data.description: Phenylethanoid glycoside from Forsythiae Fructus that binds ASCL1 and blocks a downstream CCNB1/mTOR axis.

page_status.reason: By design: fewer than three linked studies and not a node on the pathway map, so no page is generated. The record is still served here and in the bulk exports.

data.description_beginner: A compound from forsythia fruit, long used in traditional medicine. In lab work it sticks to the ASCL1 protein and shuts down a signalling chain that runs from there through CCNB1 to mTOR.

studies.title: Forsythoside A Alleviates Hypertensive Nephropathy by Promoting Mitophagy and Inhibiting Ferroptosis via ASCL1-CCNB1/mTOR Pathway.
studies.authors: Cui X; Yang D; Zhang Z; Wang C; Li H; Sun J; Zhang T; Wang M

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: C57BL/6 mouse; NRK-52E rat kidney cells
studies.finding: Forsythoside A binds ASCL1 and blocks the downstream CCNB1/mTOR axis, promoting mitophagy and suppressing ferroptosis to protect against Ang II-induced hypertensive nephropathy in mice — without lowering blood pressure.
